title: Avoid replacing an existing item
summary: A conditional put can require that a key does not already exist.
introduction: A conditional put can require that a key does not already exist. Your task: Try the condition with a genuinely new book key.
learningObjectives: Try the condition with a genuinely new book key.
Explain the example for avoid replacing an existing item

blocks.text: A conditional put can require that a key does not already exist. The condition is checked as part of the write.

Use DynamoDB Local and the AWS CLI or SDK in a separate practice project. Point every command at http://localhost:8000. Low-level JSON examples show request bodies; provide them to the matching CLI command or SDK method.
Read the code step by step

items: `ConditionExpression` checks the current item as part of the write, so a failed condition prevents the change.
`attribute_not_exists` requires that the named attribute is absent at the targeted item key.
`ExpressionAttributeNames` maps placeholders such as #reader to actual field names in the request expression.

blocks.text: The write fails with a condition error if that exact key already has an item.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A condition failure is an expected outcome to handle, not a reason to retry the same forbidden overwrite forever.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Try the condition with a genuinely new book key.
